comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: This looks like it has interesting combat and would love to know about the story and lore. But does it "Look like AI?" If you hadn't told me I (or posted this forum) it would not have been my first thought. But let's not make "not look like AI" the goal. This looks like a great start, keep going!

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Yes, it looks quite bad.

 \- Showcase the gameplay. I have literally no idea what type of game this is from the trailer or what I would be doing in it. ...Are people having the machine build these trailers? Is that why they all have such bizarre footage choices? 

 \- The look is very stilted and floaty. Honestly, that's not per se an AI problem or an indicator, but it does look bad and makes me uninterested in the experience. 

 \- The combat just looks totally horrible and boring. There's no motion, no weight, nothing. You feature characters basically just standing in place and swishing around attacks while using oversaturated attack footprint indicators. 

  
I don't know that there is anything in particular that I could point to as something to change. The game needs a lot more work before you showcase it, and the trailer needs to do the game more favours.

comments.author: Lambisexual
comments.body:
Yes. It is. But there's potential, so don't be disheartened. I think the player model looks pretty cute/charming. Same with the Countess. I just think you constructed a game that doesn't really fit the style. 

Animations are the biggest weak point currently. Like your character just wiggling back and forth as they slash in front of them looks really awkward. And combat as a whole just looks floaty with very predictable NPC behaviour/movement from the enemies. It looks like it want to be a bit flashy and fast, but simultaneously plays very slowly. 

You should have thought a bit more about how stiff your characters look, and either construct a game around that fact so it's not a problem, or fix that problem before constructing the game that depends on it. 

For instance, you could've made it an entire theme of the game that the characters are like dolls and toys and such (not necessarily in a childish way. It can still have a gritty or more mature theme if you want). Cause then the stiff movements would actually play into the identity of the world/characters.
